description: A Junior CS major with a strong background in systems security who prefers building and breaking things over theoretical modeling.

nodes.personalizationRationale: For a student with strong prior exposure, we begin with a concise review of OS foundations to establish a baseline for advanced architectural analysis.
nodes.description: Examine the architecture of modern operating systems, focusing on the separation of kernel and user modes and the interface provided by system calls.
nodes.title: OS Architecture & System Calls
Advanced System Structures & Design Tradeoffs
nodes.personalizationRationale: This student's strong prior exposure allows for a deeper dive into OS design tradeoffs and structural optimization early in the course.
nodes.description: Compare monolithic, microkernel, and hybrid OS structures, analyzing performance implications and modularity tradeoffs in production kernels like Linux or Mach.
Review process states, PCB structure, and the mechanics of context switching within the operating system kernel.
nodes.personalizationRationale: Leveraging this student's strong prior exposure, this node focuses on the low-level implementation details of the process abstraction.
nodes.title: Process Management & Implementation
IPC Performance & Shared Memory Optimization
nodes.personalizationRationale: Since the student has strong prior exposure, we explore advanced IPC performance optimizations rather than basic socket programming.
nodes.description: Analyze high-performance IPC mechanisms, including shared memory synchronization and zero-copy message passing techniques used in distributed systems.

nodes.title: Multicore Threading Models
nodes.description: Differentiate between user-level and kernel-level threads and evaluate threading libraries like Pthreads in multi-core environments.
nodes.personalizationRationale: Given the student's strong prior exposure, this node builds on their knowledge of threading to analyze multicore scalability issues.
Strong prior exposure allows the student to quickly master scheduling criteria and apply them to complex system evaluation scenarios.
nodes.description: Compare CPU scheduling algorithms like Round Robin, Priority, and Multi-level Feedback Queues against real-world workload requirements.
nodes.title: CPU Scheduling Policy & Evaluation
Midterm Review Assessment (Ch 1-5)
nodes.personalizationRationale: This required assessment ensures the student with strong prior exposure has correctly mapped their background knowledge to the specific course learning objectives.
nodes.description: Synthesize material from OS Foundations through CPU Scheduling in preparation for the midterm exam.

nodes.title: Primitives & Classic Sync Problems
nodes.description: Solve classic synchronization problems like the Bounded-Buffer and Dining Philosophers using mutexes, semaphores, and monitors.
nodes.personalizationRationale: With strong prior exposure, the student will focus on the formal verification of synchronization primitives and avoiding common pitfalls.
Strong prior exposure justifies an enrichment node focused on advanced lock-free programming techniques used in modern kernel development.
nodes.description: Examine lock-free data structures, atomic operations, and memory consistency models in modern multi-threaded systems.
nodes.title: Lock-Free Sync & Memory Consistency
Deadlock Characterization & Prevention
nodes.description: Analyze the four necessary conditions for deadlock and methods for prevention through static resource ordering.
nodes.personalizationRationale: This node provides core theory on deadlock characterization, which remains essential regardless of the student's strong prior exposure.

nodes.title: Deadlock Avoidance & Detection Models
nodes.description: Implement and analyze the Banker’s Algorithm for deadlock avoidance and resource-allocation graphs for detection.
nodes.personalizationRationale: Even with strong prior exposure, mastering the analytical modeling of resource allocation is a core requirement for OS design.

nodes.description: Detailed study of paging, page table structures (hierarchical, hashed, inverted), and the role of the TLB in address translation.
nodes.personalizationRationale: Strong prior exposure enables this student to focus on the hardware-software interface and complexity of multi-level page tables.
nodes.title: Paging & Address Translation Mechanics
Demand Paging & Replacement Policies
nodes.personalizationRationale: This core node is critical for the memory management project, ensuring the student's strong prior exposure translates to practical implementation.
nodes.description: Implement demand paging and evaluate page replacement algorithms like LRU and Optimal under varying memory pressure.

nodes.title: Cache Interaction & Advanced Thrashing Analysis
nodes.description: Investigate the interaction between OS page replacement and hardware cache hierarchies to mitigate thrashing.
nodes.personalizationRationale: For a student with strong prior exposure, we add enrichment on the performance impacts of cache locality and hardware-aware memory management.

nodes.description: Explore I/O hardware, interrupt-driven I/O vs. DMA, and the structure of the kernel I/O subsystem.
nodes.personalizationRationale: Strong prior exposure ensures the student can efficiently navigate I/O subsystem design and its impact on overall system performance.
nodes.title: I/O Subsystems & Performance Drivers

nodes.personalizationRationale: This core node ensures the student understands the persistent storage abstractions required for the final examination and projects.
nodes.description: Contrast file allocation methods (contiguous, linked, indexed) and their impact on disk performance and reliability.
nodes.title: File System Implementation & Reliability Bonds

nodes.personalizationRationale: This mandatory assessment verifies that the student has integrated their strong prior exposure with the specific advanced topics covered in the course.
nodes.description: Comprehensive review and assessment of all course topics from process management through file systems for the cumulative final exam.
nodes.title: Cumulative Final Review & Assessment
